evals.prompt: We publish comparison articles about payroll software. Our pages rank on page one but Perplexity and ChatGPT keep citing competitors instead. Audit this page structure and tell me what to change: [paste page text]
evals.expected_output: A pass/fail table against the Step 11 checklist, fixes classified by layer (Access first), the top three changes most likely to move citation share, every recommendation carrying a G/I/P/S evidence label, and no claims that schema or llms.txt alone will fix it.

evals.prompt: Write an outline and the opening 200 words for a page answering 'What is a fiduciary financial advisor?' that works for Google, AI Overviews, voice assistants, and Perplexity.
evals.expected_output: Target query and 20-35 word answer sentence stated first; a 40-75 word answer block at the top; H2s phrased as fan-out sub-questions; a comparison table plan with prose summary; visible FAQ; author byline and sources; note on balanced language for regulated content.

evals.prompt: Our agency says we need FAQ schema, HowTo schema, and an llms.txt file to show up in AI search. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: States that FAQ rich results ended May 7, 2026 and HowTo in 2023 (markup still valid, no Google effect); cites Google's May 2026 guide saying llms.txt and special schema are not needed for its AI features; labels the agency's claim [I] with no primary support; recommends Article/Person/Organization schema and visible Q&A content; separates the training-bot decision from citation.

evals.prompt: Set up a way for us to track whether we're being cited by AI engines. We have Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, and GA4 but no paid tools.
evals.expected_output: Minimum viable stack: Search Console Generative AI report, Bing AI Performance report, GA4 referrer segments, server-log user-agent counts, and a fixed 20-prompt weekly panel with a logging template; reports share of AI voice rather than raw counts; benchmarks labeled [I].
